{{Nihongo|'''Susumu Kitagawa''' {{Post-nominals|country=GBR|FRS}}|北川 進|Kitagawa Susumu|born 4 July 1951}} is a Japanese [[Nobel Prize in Chemistry|Nobel Prize]]-winning [[chemist]] specializing in [[coordination chemistry]], with a focus on organic–inorganic hybrid compounds and the chemical and physical properties of [[porous medium|porous]] coordination polymers, particularly [[metal-organic framework]]s.<ref name=AngewChem2009>{{cite journal|title=Susumu Kitagawa|date=9 November 2009|journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition|volume=48|issue=47|pages=8818–8820|doi=10.1002/anie.200904270 |bibcode=2009ACIE...48.8818. }}</ref> He is Distinguished Professor at [[Kyoto University]]'s Institute for Integrated Cell-Material Sciences (iCeMS), which he co-founded. In 2025, he was awarded the [[Nobel Prize in Chemistry]] jointly with [[Richard Robson (chemist)|Richard Robson]] and [[Omar M. Yaghi]].

== Life ==
[[File:20251009 Shigeru Ishiba and Susumu Kitagawa 1.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Kitagawa attended an online meeting with [[Shigeru Ishiba]] (October 9, 2025)]]
Kitagawa was born on 4 July 1951 in [[Kyoto]].<ref name=Nobel>[https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/chemistry/2025/kitagawa/facts/ Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2025 – Susumu Kitagawa]</ref>

He earned his PhD in hydrocarbon chemistry from [[Kyoto University]] in 1979, having completed his undergraduate studies at the same institution. That year, he was appointed assistant professor at [[Kindai University]], where he was promoted to lecturer in 1983 and associate professor in 1988.<ref name=AngewChem2009/><ref name=KitagawaCV2016>{{cite web|url=http://www.kitagawa.icems.kyoto-u.ac.jp/wp-content/uploads/2016/10/CV.Susumu-Kitagawa1610111.pdf|title=CV : Susumu KITAGAWA|website=Kitagawa.icems.kyoto-u.ac.jp|accessdate=12 October 2017}}</ref>

In 1992, he became professor of [[inorganic chemistry]] at [[Tokyo Metropolitan University]].<ref name=AngewChem2009/> He returned to Kyoto University in 1998 as a professor of inorganic functional chemistry in the Department of Synthetic Chemistry and [[Biochemistry|Biological Chemistry]].<ref name=KitagawaCV2016/><ref name=Trager2025/> In 2007, he co-founded the {{ill|Institute for Integrated Cell-Material Sciences|ja|物質-細胞統合システム拠点}} (iCeMS), serving as founding deputy director, then as director from 2013 to 2023.<ref name=MEXT2009>{{Cite web |title=物質-細胞統合システム拠点（iCeMS） 1拠点構想等の概要（京都大学） |trans-title=Institute for Integrated Cell-Material Sciences (iCeMS): Overview of the Center Initiative (Kyoto University) |language=ja |work=[[Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology]] |date=2009 |access-date=11 October 2025 |url= https://www.mext.go.jp/a_menu/kagaku/toplevel/07120413/003.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090509221335/http://www.mext.go.jp/a_menu/kagaku/toplevel/07120413/003.htm |archive-date=9 May 2009}}</ref><ref name=icemsTimeline>{{cite web |title=Timeline |url=https://www.icems.kyoto-u.ac.jp/en/about/timeline |website=Institute for Integrated Cell-Material Sciences |access-date=11 October 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250710081421/https://www.icems.kyoto-u.ac.jp/en/about/timeline/ |archive-date=10 July 2025}}</ref> In 2024, he was appointed Executive Vice-President for Research Promotion at Kyoto University.<ref name=KUIAS-profile>{{cite web |title=Profile: Susumu Kitagawa |url=https://kuias.kyoto-u.ac.jp/e/profile/kitagawa |website=Kyoto University Institute for Advanced Study |access-date=12 October 2025 |language=en}}</ref>

His overseas academic postings include a postdoctoral fellowship at [[Texas A&M University]] with [[F. Albert Cotton]] (1986–1987) and a guest professorship at the [[City University of New York]] (1996).<ref name=AngewChem2009/><ref name=Trager2025/><ref name=Kitagawa2001>{{cite book |author-last=Kitagawa |author-first=Susumu |title=集積型金属錯体<!--[[:ja:%E9%9B%86%E7%A9%8D%E5%9E%8B%E9%87%91%E5%B1%9E%E9%8C%AF%E4%BD%93]]-->: クリスタルエンジニアリングからフロンティアオービタルエンジニアリングへ |trans-title=Supramolecular Metal Complexes: From Crystal Engineering to Frontier Orbital Engineering |publisher=[[Kodansha]] |date=20 June 2001 |isbn=978-4-06-153395-0 |url=https://www.kinokuniya.co.jp/f/dsg-01-9784061533950 |language=ja |access-date=11 October 2025}}</ref> He received an honorary doctorate from the [[Technical University of Munich]] in 2018.<ref name=TUM2025>{{cite web |title=Nobel Prize in Chemistry for TUM Honorary Doctor Kitagawa |url=https://www.tum.de/en/news-and-events/all-news/press-releases/details/nobel-prize-in-chemistry-for-tum-honorary-doctor-kitagawa |work=Technical University of Munich |access-date=11 October 2025 |date=8 October 2025}}</ref>

Kitagawa served as a member and associate member of the [[Science Council of Japan]] from 2011 to 2023.<ref name=KitagawaCV2016/><ref name=SCJ2025>{{cite web |title=日本学術会議会長談話 {{!}} 坂口志文先生のノーベル生理学・医学賞受賞、北川進先生のノーベル化学賞受賞を祝して |lang=ja |trans-title=Statement by the President of the Science Council of Japan {{!}} Congratulating Dr. Shimon Sakaguchi on winning the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine and Dr. Susumu Kitagawa on winning the Nobel Prize in Chemistry |url=https://www.scj.go.jp/ja/head/pdf/20251010.pdf |work=Science Council of Japan |date=10 October 2025 |access-date=11 October 2025}}</ref>

In 2025, Kitagawa, along with [[Richard Robson (chemist)|Richard Robson]] and [[Omar M. Yaghi]], was awarded the [[Nobel Prize in Chemistry]] for their foundational work on [[Building block (chemistry)|molecular building blocks]] for metal-organic frameworks.<ref name="NYT2025ChemistryNobel">{{cite web | last1=Robles-Gil | first1=Alexa | last2=Watkins | first2=Ali | title=Nobel Prize in Chemistry Awarded to Architects of Metal-Organic Frameworks | website=The New York Times | date=2025-10-08 | url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/10/08/science/nobel-prize-chemistry.html | access-date=2025-10-08}}</ref>

== Research ==
{{Scholia}}
Following the discoveries of [[Makoto Fujita (chemist)|Makoto Fujita]] (1994) and [[Omar M. Yaghi]] (1995), Kitagawa demonstrated in 1997 that coordination polymer structures possess gas adsorption properties, a key finding for the development of functional porous materials.<ref name=Trager2025>{{Cite web |title=Meet the three scientists who have just won the Nobel prize in chemistry |author=Rebecca Trager |work=[[Chemistry World]] |date=9 October 2025 |access-date=11 October 2025 |url=https://www.chemistryworld.com/news/meet-the-three-scientists-who-have-just-won-the-nobel-prize-in-chemistry/4022291.article |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251011003820/https://www.chemistryworld.com/news/meet-the-three-scientists-who-have-just-won-the-nobel-prize-in-chemistry/4022291.article |archive-date=11 October 2025}}</ref>

His most influential works include:
*A 1997 seminal report on a porous coordination polymer (MOF) for small molecule adsorption.<ref name=AngewChem2009/><ref name=Koester2005>{{cite web |last1=Koester |first1=Vera |title=Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2025 |url=https://www.chemistryviews.org/nobel-prize-in-chemistry-2025/ |work=[[ChemistryViews]] |date=8 October 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |doi=10.1002/anie.199717251 |volume=36 |issue=16 |title=Three-Dimensional Framework with Channeling Cavities for Small Molecules: <math chem>\ce{{[M2(4, 4'-bpy)3(NO3)4].\mathit{x}H2O}_\mathit{n}\ \ (M = Co, Ni, Zn)}</math> |journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition |pages=1725–1727 |year=1997 |last1=Kondo |first1=Mitsuru |last2=Yoshitomi |first2=Tomomichi |last3=Matsuzaka |first3=Hiroyuki |last4=Kitagawa |first4=Susumu |last5=Seki |first5=Kenji }}</ref>
*A 2004 early review of functional porous coordination polymers.<ref name=AngewChem2009/><ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1002/anie.200300610 | volume=43 | issue=18 | title=Functional Porous Coordination Polymers | journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition | pages=2334–2375| year=2004 | last1=Kitagawa | first1=Susumu | last2=Kitaura | first2=Ryo | last3=Noro | first3=Shin-Ichiro | pmid=15114565 | bibcode=2004ACIE...43.2334K }}</ref>
*A 2009 review of "soft porous crystals," which feature large-scale structural transformability upon chemical or physical stimulation.<ref name=Koester2005/><ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1038/nchem.444 | pmid=21124356 | volume=1 | issue=9 | title=Soft porous crystals | journal=Nature Chemistry | pages=695–704| bibcode=2009NatCh...1..695H | last1=Horike | first1=Satoshi | last2=Shimomura | first2=Satoru | last3=Kitagawa | first3=Susumu | year=2009 | hdl=2433/297605 | hdl-access=free }}</ref>
